frozen_candidate_root_contribution: A vocalized burst of aversion/displeasure — the minimal audible ejaculation by which a speaker vents exasperation, irritation, or repugnance toward the person or thing it is aimed at.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: A vocalized burst of aversion/displeasure — the minimal audible ejaculation by which a speaker vents exasperation, irritation, or repugnance toward the person or thing it is aimed at.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The root surfaces in all three occurrences as one and the same lexical interjection, أُفٍّ ("uff"), an exclamatory noise of displeasure. In 17:23 the son is forbidden to so much as say أُفٍّ to aged parents ("فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفٍّ") — here the utterance is the smallest conceivable audible sign of impatience/annoyance, set in a chain with تَنْهَرْهُمَا (rebuking) as an escalation of the same aversion. In 21:67 Abraham hurls "أُفٍّ لَّكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ" at his people and their idols — the same interjection venting disgust/repudiation. In 46:17 the impious son answers his parents "أُفٍّ لَّكُمَآ أَتَعِدَانِنِىٓ..." — venting exasperated rejection at their warning of resurrection. Across mild filial impatience (17:23), prophetic contempt (21:67), and rebellious exasperation (46:17), the invariant the root itself supplies is the spontaneous expulsion of displeasure as a cry — not a proposition, not a verb of action, but an affect-laden exclamation of aversion.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: uniform — all 3 are tag "N", the frozen interjection/ism أُفٍّ (with tanwīn); no verb, participle, or productive verbal-noun derivation to subtract. CONSTRUCTION: near-uniform — the interjection optionally governs a dative لـ naming the target of displeasure (لَّهُمَآ 17:23, لَّكُمْ 21:67, لَّكُمَآ 46:17); the لـ supplies the 'directed-at' vector, not the aversion itself. PARTICIPANTS: vary — target is parents (17:23, 46:17) or a people together with their false gods (21:67); speaker is a hypothetical child, a rebellious son, or the prophet Abraham. CONTEXT: varies — filial-piety ethics (17:23), anti-idolatry rebuke (21:67), denial-of-resurrection narrative (46:17). Subtracting the (invariant) interjectional form, the (near-invariant) dative frame, the varying participants, and the varying context leaves exactly one residue: the vocalized venting of aversion/displeasure.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 17:23 is the hardest case because the displeasure there is minimal and directed at beloved, honored parents — closer to weary impatience than to the contempt seen in 21:67/46:17. It reconciles cleanly: the verse works precisely by treating أُفٍّ as the smallest possible audible expression of displeasure (its prohibition is a fortiori — if even that tiny vent is barred, harsher speech certainly is). Far from breaking the core, it fixes the lower bound of the same aversion-venting residue.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative core is "contempt / repudiation of the addressee," which fits 21:67 (idolaters) and 46:17 (rejecting resurrection) well. Internal evidence arbitrates against it: 17:23 forbids أُفٍّ toward parents in a context of mandated iḥsān (kindness), where the speaker is not expressing contempt but momentary impatience. Only the broader reading — "vented displeasure/aversion of variable intensity, from mild irritation to disgust" — covers all three; contempt is one high-intensity instance, not the invariant.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest neighbors: (1) نهر n-h-r "rebuke/repel," which appears in the very same verse (17:23 وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا) — نهر is a transitive verbal act of driving-back/scolding, whereas أُفٍّ is a non-propositional interjection venting inner displeasure, showing the two are lexically distinct even in one breath; (2) غضب gh-ḍ-b "wrath," a sustained affective state, versus أُفٍّ as a momentary spontaneous ejaculation; (3) كره k-r-h "to find hateful/aversion," an evaluative attitude rather than an audible cry. Falsifiability: if any occurrence used أُفٍّ in a neutral, approving, or purely descriptive frame (e.g., as a name, or expressing satisfaction), the aversion-venting core would be falsified. No such case exists in the data.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty contribution — the vocalized venting of aversion/displeasure — is surface-recoverable in every one of the 3 occurrences. The root manifests as exactly one lexeme (the interjection أُفٍّ) in one form family, with a near-uniform dative construction, so there is minimal derivational or constructional noise to strip away. The direction is determinate (aversion expelled outward toward a named target) and sharply distinct from neighboring roots for rebuking (نهر), wrath (غضب), and disliking (كره), one of which sits adjacently in 17:23 without merging. The only internal variation is intensity — mild impatience (17:23) to contempt (21:67, 46:17) — which is a scalar range within the same affect, not a break in the core, and is resolved by the broader "displeasure" reading over the narrower "contempt" competitor. No occurrence resists the residue; hence clean universal presence and STRONG strength.

adversarial_verification.notes: Refutation attempt failed to break the unity. All 3 occurrences are literally the identical lexical interjection أُفٍّ (packet form_inventory: single form N, count 3), each an affect-laden non-propositional cry venting displeasure at a target. 17:23 (filial impatience toward aged parents, escalated by تَنْهَرْهُمَا), 21:67 (Abraham's disgust/repudiation of people+idols), 46:17 (son's exasperated rejection of parents' resurrection warning) differ only in intensity and target, not in the root-supplied invariant. Hardest angle tried was over-breadth: rejected because the candidate is tethered specifically to aversion/displeasure, not any emotion, and excludes verbs of action and approval/summons particles. Neighbor-root contrast: discriminates cleanly from other interjection roots (approval, pain/lament, summons) and from any action-verb reading. Falsifiable via clear conditions (approval use, neutral address, verbal action) none of which occur. No semantic split or homonymy exists to exploit.

occurrence_dispositions.note: أُفٍّ in فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفٍّ — the forbidden minimal audible cry of impatience/annoyance toward aged parents, chained with تَنْهَرْهُمَا as escalation; the affect-laden ejaculation of aversion is directly present.
أُفٍّ لَّكُمْ hurled by Abraham at his people and their idols — the same exclamatory burst venting disgust/repudiation; candidate residue of vocalized aversion recovered.
أُفٍّ لَّكُمَآ spoken by the impious son to his parents, venting exasperated rejection of their warning; the spontaneous cry of displeasure is exactly the invariant supplied by the root.
